messages:
PagerBot: INCIDENT ALERT - KV_CACHE_EVICTION_SPIKE detected on shards in us-west-2 (>= 3x baseline). auto-page: on
Maya: I'm paged, looking now. seeing eviction rate jump and continuous-batch windows growing.
Kevin: paging in — what customer impact? any 5xxs or high p95?
Maya: p95 token latency up from 120ms -> 650ms for some tenants. 2 customers reporting degraded responses (AcmeCorp, beta-17). no widespread 5xx yet.
Olivia: logs show batch-window sizing increasing, kv-cache miss amplification. suspect change from last night's batch-window tweak (feature flag: dynamic_batch_window=true).
Sam: I can jump on a call in 2 mins. are we rolling back the flag?
Maya: hold — want to confirm scope first. Sam, can you pull per-tenant cache evictions?
Sam: running query :
```
SELECT tenant_id, sum(evictions) as ev, avg(batch_window_ms) as bw
FROM metrics.kv_cache
WHERE ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY ev DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Sam: results: AcmeCorp ev=18k bw=420ms, beta-17 ev=9k bw=380ms, others trending up but <1k ev.
Leah (SRE): tagging as P2 because customer-visible degradation and potential cost blast. recommend per-customer mitigation for the two highest tenants + canary rollback for flag.
Kevin: agreed. Maya - can we flip per-customer override for AcmeCorp and beta-17 to legacy batch window (dynamic_batch_window=false) while we stage a canary rollback for everyone?
Maya: yes. I have the oncall runbook open. Per-customer override endpoint is `POST /v1/flags/override`.
Maya: applying override for AcmeCorp now:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/flags/override \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"flag":"dynamic_batch_window","tenant":"acmecorp","value":false,"reason":"eviction spike"}'
```
DeployBot: override accepted. Active on 2 routing nodes for tenant acmecorp (propagation ~15s).
Olivia: applying for beta-17 too.
Olivia: override applied for tenant beta-17. Observability: evictions down by ~30% in first 45s. p95 latency dropping.
Maya: good. now prepping a canary rollback of the global flag to false. plan: 10% of traffic -> 3 hosts in each region for 5 minutes, monitor evictions, unit-cost, and p95.
Kevin: please post the exact rollout command and who will watch. I can own the monitoring dashboard.
Maya: rollout command (internal feature-flag API):
```
POST /v1/flags/rollout
{
  "flag":"dynamic_batch_window",
  "target":"global",
  "strategy":"canary",
  "percent":10,
  "duration_minutes":5
}
```
Maya: DeployBot initiating canary now.
DeployBot: Canary started: dynamic_batch_window=false -> 10% traffic. Nodes: us-west-2-host[12-14], us-east-1-host[20-22].
Sam: monitoring logs for cache eviction churn and any error spikes. hooking into trace stream for a few flagged requests.
Leah (SRE): checklist: watchers assigned (Kevin), error budget monitor on, cost guard rails active. If evictions don't reduce by 20% in 5m, abort canary and escalate.
Kevin: dashboard linked: https://dash.internal/kv-cache?range=5m&filter=dynamic_batch_window. watching now.
Olivia: early signals: canary nodes showing 45% reduction in evictions already, p95 back to ~150ms on canary. non-canary still at ~520ms.
Maya: nice. leave canary running full 5m. I'll prepare global rollback play if needed.
(3m later)
Sam: canary halfway through, no new 5xxs, evictions trending down across canary hosts, no abnormal backend CPU.
Maya: ok if metrics hold at 5m we should promote the rollback to 50% then 100% in staged increments with 2m guard windows.
Leah (SRE): confirm promoting only if cost and latency remain stable and no new customer errors.
Maya: promoting to 50% now.
DeployBot: Promoted to 50% -> nodes updated.
Kevin: watch continues. AcmeCorp and beta-17 remain on per-customer override until global finish to avoid oscillation.
(7m later)
Olivia: after 50% promotion we saw further reduction; global eviction rate down 60% from peak. AcmeCorp latency within normal.
Maya: promoting to 100%.
DeployBot: Promoted to 100%. flag state: dynamic_batch_window=false globally.
Sam: done. rolling metrics show stabilization. opening incident timeline for postmortem.
Leah (SRE): creating incident ticket: INC-2029 with severity, timeline, root-cause hypothesis: dynamic_batch_window change interacted poorly with skewed tenant seq-len distribution causing cache amplification and batching blowup. action items: revert flag (done), add per-tenant throttle safeguards, make per-customer overrides faster (reduce propagation from 15s), add canary validator that simulates skewed seq distributions.
Maya: noted. I'll own hotfix follow-ups: add a guard in batch controller to cap batch-window growth per tenant and add a migration doc.
Kevin: I'll coordinate customer comms for AcmeCorp and beta-17 (private postmortem + status).
Olivia: posting final note: if anyone sees eviction rates climb again, flip `dynamic_batch_window` to false globally and follow same staged rollout.
PagerBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - KV_CACHE_EVICTION_SPIKE (resolved by flag rollback & per-tenant overrides).
Maya: thanks all. handoff to night oncall: @Olivia you'll take remaining follow-ups?
Olivia: yup, taking handoff. leaving notes in the incident ticket.
Leah (SRE): great work. rough 28m incident. we'll schedule a blameless postmortem and link this thread.
